stem: During prospective review a Massachusetts pharmacist identifies a therapeutic duplication, telephones the prescriber, agrees a change to the therapy, and dispenses the revised prescription. She makes no note of the call, on the basis that the clinical issue was fully resolved before anything was dispensed. What remains outstanding?

choices.text: Nothing; resolving the issue clinically discharges what the regulation requires.
A report of the therapeutic duplication to the Board of Registration in Pharmacy.
A second prospective review of the revised therapy before it is dispensed.
Written confirmation from the prescriber of the change that was agreed.
Documentation of the measures she took in response to the review.

explanation.core_reasoning: 247 CMR 9.17(2) leaves the choice of responsive measure open, offering consultation with the prescriber or with the patient as examples, but then provides that a pharmacist SHALL DOCUMENT ANY MEASURES TAKEN in response to a drug utilization review. The documentation duty is unconditional and is not discharged by resolving the underlying problem.

choice_analysis.A: The paragraph imposes a separate documentation duty.
choice_analysis.B: No report to the Board is required.
choice_analysis.C: No second review is required by the paragraph.
choice_analysis.D: Written prescriber confirmation is not what the paragraph requires.
choice_analysis.E: Correct: the measures taken must be documented.

related_facts: Consultation with the prescriber is an example rather than the required measure
explanation.mpje_trap: Candidates treat a resolved clinical problem as a closed file and overlook the freestanding record duty.

reasoning_steps: Separate the discretionary choice of measure from the mandatory record of it
Note that the pharmacist did take an appropriate measure
Identify the documentation duty as the one left unperformed
